Question: Polynomials \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) each have degree \(3\) and leading coefficient \(1,\) and their roots are all elements of \(\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}.\) The function \(f(x) = \dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) has the property that there exist real numbers \(a \lt b \lt c \lt d\) such that the set of all real numbers \(x\) such that \(f(x) \le 0\) consists of the closed interval \([a, b]\) together with the open interval \((c, d).\) How many functions \(f(x)\) are possible?
